**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The vendor warranty package in Section 9(b) meets or exceeds the preferred position:

- **Performance standard** — the Service "will perform in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034) and services "shall be free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038).
- **No malicious code** — express virus/Trojan/worm/backdoor warranty (p0036).
- **Compliance with laws** — warranted throughout the Term (p0041).
- **Duration** — better than preferred: these are continuing Term-long warranties, not a 90-day or 12-month window.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow it** — Section 13's "as is" language is expressly qualified by "Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement" (p0062), so the express warranties survive intact.

The one gap versus the model language is the absence of a stated repair/replace/refund remedy. I deliberately did not flag this: the agreement imposes no exclusive-remedy limitation, so we keep the full range of contractual remedies, including termination for uncured material breach on 30 days' notice. Inserting the playbook's remedy sentence would risk *narrowing* our position rather than improving it. Noted in the rationale as a sub-element only.
